title: The Poor Boy in the Grave

keywords: the poor boy in the grave
full_text:
A poor orphan boy was apprenticed to a cruel, hard-hearted farmer and his equally spiteful wife. From morning till dusk, the child was forced to chop heavy timber, clean stables in the freezing snow, and eat moldy crusts, suffering harsh blows for the slightest accident.

One day, the farmer sent the shivering lad to carry a jar of sweet oil to the cellar. Tripping over an icy stone, the jar shattered on the floor. Fearing the farmer's brutal beating, the boy fled into the orchard and hid beneath a barrel of vinegar. When the farmer discovered him, he beat the orphan mercilessly with an ox-hide whip.

Despairing of any mercy in this earthly life, the child saw a jar marked 'Poison' in the pantry—which the farmer had actually filled with sweet honey to keep it safe from thieves. Wishing only for peaceful sleep, the boy ate the entire jar and lay down in an open grave dug in the quiet churchyard, crossing his hands and waiting to die.

Instead of dying of poison, the sweet honey warmed his chilled body and filled him with peaceful dreams. The village pastor found the sleeping child, took him into his warm parsonage, and heard the full tale of the farmer's cruelty. The magistrates stripped the farmer of his wealth to pay for the boy's education, and the gentle orphan grew into a prosperous, compassionate scholar who dedicated his life to protecting the weak.
moral: Cruelty to the defenseless cries out for justice, and peace awaits the pure in heart.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
